# Plan: Greek Revival plantation house on the river ("plantation")

Identity: an Oak Alley-type antebellum mansion. A broad white two-storey block, raised on a red-brick base, fronted by eight colossal white columns
(2x2, 13 high) across a full-width double gallery. The gallery has an upper porch floor and white balustrades, and it all sits under one low slate hip
with a quartz dentil cornice, three front dormers and four brick chimneys. Tall black-shuttered windows, a wide central hall with a fanlit double door
on both floors. A rear T-wing holds a two-storey vaulted living room open to the kitchen. The grounds run from a gravel drive under an allee of eight
spreading live oaks to an oval forecourt. On the west is a formal boxwood parterre with a fountain, a glass greenhouse, and a white gazebo on the riverbank. On the east are a brick carriage house with a cupola,
a white guest cottage (the house in miniature), and flowering cherries on the lawns. At the back, a lawn runs to the river and a landing dock.

Site x 0..95, z 0..95, y -4..32. Front = NORTH (z0 = the county road edge). Ground: grass top at y0 (player stands y1). All ranges inclusive.
House: base y0..2, GROUND FLOOR y3 (stand y4), air y4..9, UPPER FLOOR y10 (stand y11), air y11..16, wall plate / gallery ceiling y17, roofs y18+.
House axis of symmetry x = 47.5 (pairs mirror as x <-> 95-x). Later parts only ADD into air: every opening/reserved cell below is left AIR by the shell.

input.concept_subject: An Oak Alley-style antebellum plantation estate on the Mississippi bank. A grand drive of gravel runs south from a white picket fence and brick gate piers (lanterns on quartz caps) between two files of four enormous live oaks. Their dark-green domed crowns meet overhead, with Spanish moss hanging from them, and they open onto an oval forecourt with an azalea-ringed urn. Straight ahead stands a broad white two-storey Greek Revival mansion on a red-brick raised base with arched iron vents. Eight colossal white quartz columns, with Ionic capitals, stand across a full-width double gallery with white balustrades on both floors. Behind them is a white wall with tall black-shuttered floor-length windows and a fanlit double black door on both floors. A cream-white dentil cornice crowns it, and a low slate hip roof with three gabled dormers on the front and four tall brick chimneys rises above. At the back a T-wing carries the vaulted living room and kitchen to a small porch with slim columns, then a lawn runs to a sand bank, the river and a spruce dock. West of the house is a formal boxwood parterre with a quartz-ringed fountain, a glasshouse and a white octagonal gazebo with a dark cap on the riverbank. East is a red-brick carriage house with a white cupola and three arched doors on a gravel yard, a miniature white guest cottage with a four-column porch, and pink flowering cherry trees on the lawns.
